defects.summary: #124's new guard can be silently and completely disarmed by an ordinary shell construct: `_strip_heredocs` reads an unquoted here-string (`<<<word`) as a heredoc opener and blanks every line from there to the end of the step, and the negative control written to prevent exactly this does not catch it.
defects.evidence:
The opener regex is `<<-?\s*(['"]?)([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)\1` searched on each line. On `cat <<<HELLO` it matches starting at the SECOND `<`, takes `HELLO` as the delimiter, and blanks the rest of the body because no line ever equals `HELLO`. `n=$((1<<shift))` does the same with delimiter `shift`. Live, in the shipped file: splice

          if grep -q fresh <<<yes; then
            echo matched
          fi
          mkdir -p ../scratch

above `case "$verdict" in` and the WHOLE FILE stays green - 289 passed. `_classified()` returns 47 commands ending at `(248, 'if grep -q fresh <<<yes; then', True)`; the added `mkdir` is absent, the `case` block is absent, and the `$GITHUB_OUTPUT` write is absent. A bare `mkdir` is verbatim the fault 58cfab6 fixed and the reason this class exists. `test_the_classifier_reads_every_line_of_the_step` cannot see it: its check is `assert not line.strip() or number in covered` against `_shell_scan(_strip_heredocs(body))`, and over-blanked lines ARE blank, so the classifier that sees nothing certifies everything - the exact sentence in that test's own docstring. Control that the mutation is otherwise detectable: the same `mkdir` spliced without the here-string reds `test_every_command_that_can_fail_sits_in_an_if_or_an_or_list`. Neither `<<<` nor the `$(( x<<n ))` shift is named in `_strip_heredocs`' docstring.

defects.summary: #124's carve-out is broader than both the list documenting it and the workflow paragraph citing it: `command.startswith("echo")` exempts an entire PIPELINE headed by `echo`, and any command whose name merely begins with "echo". A pipeline that aborts the step under `bash -e` passes the new guard.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:1640 - `if command.startswith("echo") and not redirects: return True`. Measured in bash: `set -uo pipefail` + `echo hi | grep -q zzz` under `bash -e` exits 1 and never reaches the next line, so it aborts the step exactly like a bare `mkdir`. Spliced into the audit step above the `case`, `test_every_command_that_can_fail_sits_in_an_if_or_an_or_list` PASSES (4 passed). Same for `echo x | tee /tmp/zz`, `echo x | python3 -c "import sys;sys.exit(1)"`, and for `echofail` / `echoes_are_bad --now` - a bare failable command carved out on a prefix match. Both descriptions of the carve-out say something narrower than the code: the list at :1611 says "an `echo` to stdout - an `echo` to a runner's stdout essentially never fails. An `echo` that REDIRECTS is a different command and gets no carve-out here", and .github/workflows/account-skill-zips.yml:199-203 tells the reader the test "reds ... on any command sitting outside an `if` condition and a `||` list that is not in that test's own commented carve-out list". A pipeline is in neither description and is admitted anyway. The `<`/`>` redirect test also cannot see `|`.

defects.summary: `_uncomment` builds a fresh `_WordParens` per LINE, so a `)` closing a multi-line `$( )` reads as an operator and it strips code bash runs - while `_shell_scan`, which walks the whole body with one instance, gets it right. The two scanners drift on exactly the shape round 2's defect was about, and the comment added to rule that out says the opposite.

A `case` pattern `)` inside a command substitution pops the substitution's own stack entry, so BOTH scanners then read the substitution's closing `)#` as a comment opener - inventing a comment where bash sees data, which is the direction `_WordParens`' docstring names as the more expensive one and does not disclose.

`_WordParens`' docstring asserts a coverage claim that is false, in the branch whose subject is exactly that: it names six `)` shapes and says every one of them is executed in a real bash, but two of them have no script in the table and the coverage test cannot notice.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:79-82: "Neither direction is asserted in this comment. Every shape named above is executed in a real bash by test_bash_opens_a_comment_only_after_a_paren_that_ends_a_word." The shapes named above it are: a `case` pattern terminator, a subshell or group close, an arithmetic `))`, A FUNCTION DEFINITION'S PARAMETER LIST, a command substitution `$( )`, and a process substitution `<( )` / `>( )`. `_COMMENT_OPENER_SCRIPTS` (:1146-1173) has no script for the function-definition parameter list and none for `>( )` - its process-substitution entry is `<(`. Both shapes in fact agree with the model (measured: `foo()#; echo LOUD\n{ echo DONE; }\nfoo` opens a comment in bash, `_shell_scan` and `_uncomment`; `echo hi | tee >(cat >/dev/null)#; echo LOUD` opens one in none of the three) - so what is wrong is the claim, not the rule. test_every_opener_this_file_models_is_executed_by_the_table cannot catch it: it checks only the characters in `_COMMENT_OPENS_AFTER`, the index-0 case, and that both booleans of the `)` rule appear somewhere - a claim about six named SHAPES is outside everything it asserts.

defects.summary: The comment justifying the three wrapped-warning fixtures claims each catches a model the others do not, and its own table three lines below says otherwise - measured, two of the three are strictly redundant for model discrimination, so the test cited as making them "undeletable for the right reason" does not.
defects.evidence: scripts/test_account_workflows.py:996-997: "THE THREE WRAPPED SHAPES DISCRIMINATE THE THREE QUOTE MODELS `_shell_scan` rejects, and each is here for a model the others do not catch." The table immediately below already contradicts it - `#-before-the-closing-quote` reds two models, the other two red "per-line masking alone". Executed at HEAD across all four scanners (real, per-line-quotes, strip-then-mask, mask-then-strip): wrapped-warning-hash-before-the-closing-quote reds per-line-quotes AND strip-then-mask; wrapped-warning-with-no-hash reds per-line-quotes only; wrapped-warning-hash-with-the-quote-closing-later reds per-line-quotes only; apostrophe-inside-a-comment reds mask-then-strip only. So the second and third catch nothing the first does not. `_MODEL_PAIRINGS` asserts only the positive pairings, never the "alone", and test_each_rejected_quote_model_is_caught_by_its_own_fixture's docstring ("THIS IS WHAT MAKES THE THREE WRAPPED SHAPES UNDELETABLE FOR THE RIGHT REASON. Without it they look like three near-duplicates of one another") is therefore the same unbacked claim - for model coverage they are near-duplicates, and deleting two costs nothing that this test measures.
